draft:
We are seeing increasing opportunity in European clinical decision support software. The category — software that helps clinicians make better, faster, more consistent treatment decisions at the point of care — is at a structural inflection point driven by three forces.

First, the regulatory pathway under EU MDR has matured. Incumbents with serious clinical software have built up meaningful regulatory clearances, creating real barriers to entry. Second, payer willingness to reimburse digital health products has improved markedly across the major European markets. Third, generative AI is creating both an opportunity and a competitive pressure: opportunity for products that genuinely improve clinical workflows, pressure on incumbents who lack credible AI strategies.

The European market is structurally distinct from the US in ways that favour a thoughtful financial sponsor. National payers create clearer routes to scale once adopted by a national authority. The competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets, with leaders in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics but few players with meaningful pan-European presence — creating conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.

We are currently in advanced discussions with a German market leader and expect to bring a specific transaction memo to the Committee within six weeks. The target has approximately EUR 35 million of ARR growing at 22 percent annually, with very high gross retention and a strong existing MDR clearance position.
